chunks: And Zurārah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A man does not leave behind anything more burdensome upon him than silent wealth.
He said: I said to him, “What should he do?”
He said: “He should place it in a walled garden, an orchard, and a house.”

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, Imam Jaʿfar al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الْحَائِطِ: a walled garden or enclosed property
key_terms.الْمَالِ الصَّامِتِ: silent wealth, meaning inactive or unproductive wealth
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurārah, the narrator transmitting this hadith

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about leaving behind idle wealth?
ai.summary: The hadith teaches that unused and stagnant wealth can become a burden upon a person after death. It directs that wealth should be placed into beneficial, productive property rather than left idle, reflecting responsible conduct in livelihood and wealth management.
